title: How to Transfer Domain From Godaddy to Squarespace 2026 Easily
description:
Here you will learn How to Transfer Domain From Godaddy to Squarespace 2026 Easily.

Welcome back! In today's guide, we're going to show you how to transfer a domain from GoDaddy to Squarespace. Let's get started.
 

 First, log in to your Squarespace account. If you're new to Squarespace, select ""Create Account"" and follow the instructions. Registering your domain with Squarespace streamlines the process by centralizing your website and domain settings, minimizing the hassle of managing multiple service providers.
 

 Squarespace offers built-in tools tailored for its platform, simplifying the configuration and maintenance of your domain settings without needing third-party support. Its intuitive, modern user interface makes domain management straightforward, even for those not technically inclined.
 

 To transfer your domain from GoDaddy to Squarespace, start by logging into your GoDaddy account. Click on ""Domains"" and select ""Transfer Domains."" Enter the domain you wish to transfer to Squarespace.
 

 In your GoDaddy account, navigate to ""My Products"" on the dashboard. Locate the domain you want to transfer, click ""Manage,"" and find the option to connect your domain. This allows you to forward your domain to your existing Squarespace website. Click ""Connect My Site"" to automatically redirect domain traffic to Squarespace.
 

 If you haven't registered a domain with Squarespace, you might want to search for one, but that's a topic for another video. For now, focus on transferring your domain to Squarespace.
 

 GoDaddy will handle the technical aspects, so simply click ""Connect Domain"" to make the necessary changes. For more control, you can adjust advanced settings, but if not needed, proceed by clicking ""Connect Domain.""
 

 To finalize the transfer, follow these steps: Go to Squarespace, click ""Settings,"" then ""Domains."" Choose ""Connect Third Party Domain,"" enter your domain, and select GoDaddy from the dropdown menu. Click ""Connect.""
 

 In Squarespace, navigate to ""Domain Settings,"" select ""Settings,"" then ""Domains."" Choose to register and manage domains with Squarespace or other sellers. Enter the domain you wish to use with Squarespace and follow the on-screen instructions.
 

 Should you encounter any issues transferring your domain from GoDaddy to Squarespace, visit the GoDaddy Support Center. You can contact them via phone, text, or chat for assistance. They will provide guidance on resolving any technical problems.
 

 Thank you for watching, and we'll see you in the next video!

title: Squarespace to Google Sites - How to Connect Your Domain to Google Sites Step by Step
description:
Here, you will learn how to connect a domain you bought on Squarespace to a site published on Google Sites — step-by-step and updated for 2026. This walkthrough shows the exact sequence: publish your Google Site, verify domain ownership in Google Search Console, add the required DNS records in your Squarespace domain settings, and finish the publish/redirect so visitors land on your Google Sites URL with HTTPS working. The end result: your custom domain (for example www yourdomain com ) serves your Google Site reliably and securely. 

I cover the two key DNS actions you’ll use: (1) verifying ownership (usually via a TXT record) and (2) creating the CNAME entry for www → ghs.googlehosted.com so Google can serve your site. I explain when you should use a root redirect (so example.com forwards to www example com) rather than trying to point the apex with CNAME, and why many people prefer the www + redirect approach for Google Sites. 

You’ll also get practical Squarespace steps: where to find DNS/Advanced settings, how to add or replace a CNAME record, and how to create a 301 redirect from the root if you don’t add apex records — plus tips for avoiding common errors (invalid CNAME entries, multiple conflicting records). I explain what to expect during DNS propagation, how long SSL might take to issue, and quick troubleshooting checks if the site doesn’t appear after changes. 
At the end I show how to verify HTTPS is active, test on mobile, and confirm Search Console/site publish status so search engines index your new address. The video is paced so you can follow along in real time and pause at each DNS change.
